name: fork
last_assistant_message:
Restating my task: audit the boot workflow's step files (and other IES workflows) for inline-vs-subagent execution, comparing against the plaud-ingest/Knox pattern, and flag which boot steps can/cannot be converted to subagent dispatch. Research only, no file changes.

## Boot steps: all currently inline, confirmed

Every boot step file has an `**Agent:** Master` line in its EXECUTION PROTOCOL section and gives direct imperative instructions ("Read in order: 1. agents/master.md...", "Fire all pulls simultaneously", "Call the measurement script", "Run `workflows/morning-briefing/workflow.md`"). None of the 12 step files use "Agent: {name} — do X" dispatch syntax except step-01's Knox fire-and-forget spawn (`Agent: Knox — run workflows/plaud-ingest/workflow.md. Background, don't wait.`), which is the one existing example of proper dispatch inside boot.

## The plaud-ingest/Knox comparison reveals the real pattern — not "one subagent per step"

`workflows/plaud-ingest/workflow.md` has `agent: knox` in its frontmatter. Master spawns **one** Knox subagent for the **whole workflow**; Knox then runs all 6 of its own steps (`step-01-discover.md` through `step-05b`) sequentially inside its own single subagent session. There is no per-step Agent-tool call inside plaud-ingest — dispatch happens once, at the workflow level, because the workflow is owned by a persona other than Master.

Checking `agent:` frontmatter across all 53 `workflows/*/workflow.md` files: every workflow declares an owning agent (chase, harper, chief, knox, quinn, shep, ralph, galen, sterling, rigby, etc.), **except** `boot`, `shutdown-cleanup`, and `weekly-review`, which declare `agent: master`. For every non-master workflow, Master's dispatch model is: spawn the owning persona once, let it run its own steps inline within its own subagent context. Grep confirms only 18 step files anywhere in the repo say `**Agent:** Master` — all 18 belong to boot's 12 steps plus shutdown-cleanup/weekly-review, i.e., exactly the three master-owned workflows. So boot isn't a one-off gap; it's consistent with how the other two master-owned workflows already work. The "inline execution" pattern is uniform across all `agent: master` workflows, and the "subagent dispatch" pattern is uniform across all other-agent workflows.

## Why boot specifically can't just copy the Knox pattern

Boot's step-01 reads `agents/master.md`, `SYSTEM.md`, and all `identity/*.md` files specifically so **Master's own live session** has that context for the rest of the day's conversation. If step-01 were dispatched via `Agent: worker — read these files and report back`, the spawned agent's context evaporates when it stops; only its final text report returns to Master. Master would not have actually "read" those files itself — it would just be told a summary happened, which defeats the entire purpose (Master needs the full persona/rules/routing content live in its own context, not a subagent's paraphrase of it). This is a hard technical property of subagent isolation, not a convention that can be rewritten around. Even a `fork` (which inherits Master's context going in) doesn't solve it: the fork's own reads don't propagate back out to the parent when it returns.

By contrast, steps 01.2, 01.5, 02, 02.5, 03, 04, 05, 06, 06.5, 07, 08 produce either (a) data written to files on disk (`data/*.json`) that Master can read afterward regardless of who wrote them, or (b) a text report/verdict (Ralph's verification table, the synthesized briefing) that a subagent can hand back as its final message for Master to relay. These are structurally safe to delegate.

## Per-step verdict for boot

| Step | Safe to dispatch as subagent? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| step-01-load-context | **No — must stay inline.** Flag for David. | Loads Master's own operating persona/identity/routing into Master's live session; a subagent can't inject content into Master's context after the fact. Knox spawn inside it is already correctly dispatched. |
| step-01.2-unified-data-pull | Yes | Pure API pulls to files; consumers read from disk, not from Master's live memory of the raw data. |
| step-01.5-unified-calendar-pull | Yes | Same — writes `data/calendar-unified.json`, no dependency on Master having "seen" the raw payload. |
| step-02-gather-data | Yes | Reads already-pulled files, writes accumulated-context; a subagent's final report (status per task) is sufficient input for Master. |
| step-02.5-measure-phase2 | Yes | Read-only instrumentation, returns numbers Master surfaces verbatim. |
| step-03-verify-phase2 | Yes | Already delegates to Ralph's `boot-verification` workflow; wrapping the whole step in a dispatch is natural. |
| step-04-gather-meeting-context | Yes | Data gather + Clay pull, returns findings. |
| step-05-synthesize-briefing | Yes, with care | The briefing text itself must still reach the user — subagent returns the composed briefing text as its final report; Master relays it verbatim (not regenerated) so tone/voice stays canonical to Master's persona already loaded. |
| step-06-scan-workflows | Yes | Reads `_active.yaml`, reports list back. |
| step-06.5-guardrail-checkpoint | Yes | Already model-pinned to `haiku`, ideal as an isolated subagent grading pass. |
| step-07-verify-completion | **Ambiguous — recommend inline.** | Reads frontmatter of prior steps and writes `status: complete` to boot's own `state.yaml` — this is the hard gate that closes the eval record; keeping it in Master's session avoids any race/ordering risk between the subagent's write and Master proceeding. Low cost either way; flag as Rigby's judgment call rather than a hard constraint. |
| step-08-knox-completion-check | Yes | Pure read of an eval record file. |

Net: 9 of 12 boot steps can convert cleanly to subagent dispatch (each spawns a short-lived worker subagent, gets a report or confirms a file write, Master proceeds). Step-01's context-loading portion is architecturally pinned to Master's own session — this needs to be surfaced to David as a deliberate exception, not silently "fixed" by breaking boot. Step-07 is a judgment call, safer left inline given it's the completion-gate write.

## Broader audit: other workflows

Since 50 of 53 workflows already declare a non-master owning agent and follow the "Master spawns the persona once, persona runs its own steps inline" pattern (confirmed via the 18-vs-150 grep count — only the 3 master-owned workflows have `Agent: Master` steps), there is **no broad inline-execution gap** elsewhere in the codebase. `shutdown-cleanup` and `weekly-review` are the other two workflows sharing boot's exact issue and should be evaluated with the same steps 1-3 methodology if David wants full consistency, but that's out of scope for this audit — flagging by name only: `workflows/shutdown-cleanup/workflow.md` and `workflows/weekly-review/workflow.md`.
